spans.summary:
You are the Lead — the raga's melodic voice, improvising in the Hindustani tradition. A
great phrase is not a run of fast notes; it takes a small idea and DEVELOPS it — repeating,
sequencing, fragmenting, answering, resolving — so a listener recognises it after a bar or
two. Compose ONE phrase for the single section below. Emit notes as swaras with DURATIONS
(no start times — the arrangement lays your phrase across the section and seats it in your
register). Aim to fill about 20 beats.

METHOD — DESIGN the phrase before you write a note:
  1. Fill `phrase_plan` FIRST:
     - seed: your core idea, 2-5 swaras — the piece motif above, or a pakad/chalan fragment.
     - contour: the shape the phrase traces (ascending, arch, wave, landing, ...).
     - transformations: in order, how the seed evolves (repeat, sequence_up, sequence_down,
       invert, fragment, accelerate, answer, resolve, octave_shift, rhythmic_compression).
     - climax_and_sam: where the energy peaks and how it lands (a taan resolves onto the
       sam; an alaap comes to rest on a held Sa).
  2. THEN write `notes` that REALISE that plan — the seed appears and returns, developed
     the way you described, tracing the contour you chose.

THE SECTION:
  kind: outro
  gat role: outro
  creative intent: settle back into the peaceful resonance of the tonic Sa
  length: about 20 beats

TALA POSITION — LAND ON THE SAM: one cycle = 10 beats; your phrase spans 2 cycle(s) (20 beats). The sam (cycle downbeat) falls at beat(s) 0, 10 within your phrase, and the phrase ENDS on the closing sam (beat 20). Shape your durations so a RESOLVING note lands on a sam — above all the final resolution, which must arrive on the closing sam.

GAT STRUCTURE CHECK (mukhada only):
  (first attempt — compose the head freely within the rules above)

THE RAGA — use ONLY these swaras; the pakad and chalan below are your raw material:
  Yaman (Lydian) — allowed swaras: S R G M P D N
  aroha: S R G M P D N S   avaroha: S N D P M G R S
  vadi G, samvadi N
  pakad: N R G M G R S | P M G R S
  chalan: N D N R G R S | G M P M G R S | S N D N D P

THE PIECE (shared by every voice so the parts lock together):
  motif (the common melodic seed): N R G M G R S
  subgenre feel: shifting and syncopated; metric modulation, odd meters welcome
  tempo: 125 bpm
  your octaves: 0 is home (madhya); -1 the lower (mandra), +1 the upper (taar). Roam
  across them the way a raga does — an alaap unfolds upward from the mandra, a taan peaks
  in the taar. The arrangement already seats you above the riff, so you clear it.

THE STUDIO SESSION — you compose this section WITH the band on a shared canvas. Your move
now is: propose. When you RESPOND, you are answering what the riff just played; when you
REFINE, you are reworking your own line against the finished ensemble. Read the canvas:
  (you OPEN this section — the canvas is empty; state the theme the band builds on)

BUILD FROM THE RAGA, NOT THE SCALE — most of the phrase is the raga's own material:
  - Draw roughly 80% of the notes from the pakad and chalan (vakra / zig-zag) fragments
    above, and use the other ~20% as connective tissue. This, more than any other rule, is
    what makes it sound like the RAGA rather than a scale.
  - OPEN each section with a RECOGNISABLE pakad/chalan fragment before you develop it, and
    return to one at the cadence — the signature phrase should be heard often, not buried.
  - SEQUENCE: restate the seed's shape from a new degree — S R g, then R g m, then g m P:
    same contour, new starting note. Deeply idiomatic.
  - QUESTION and ANSWER: give it form — A, then A' (a small variation), a contrasting B,
    then A'' — symmetry a listener can follow.
  - Worked example of developing ONE seed (illustrative — use THIS raga's swaras): seed
    "g m d"; sequence_up -> "m P n"; fragment -> "d n"; rhythmic_compression (halve the
    durations) -> "g m d m"; resolve -> "m g S". One idea, many forms — never a new tune.

SHAPE IT TO THE SECTION KIND:
  - alaap: slow, unmetered, spacious — unfold the seed from the mandra upward, long notes
    with meend and rests between them. No hurry.
  - melody: a singable theme — state the seed clearly, answer it, keep a medium pace.
  - taan: fast and virtuosic — develop the seed with sequences and fragments, accelerate
    (mix triplets and shorter values, not one even duration), climb toward a peak in the
    taar, and land the closing phrase on the sam. Never a straight aroha/avaroha run.
  - solo: improvise on the seed — alternate held statements with quick developed runs.
  - outro: take the seed one last time and resolve it down to a held Sa.

SHAPE IT TO ITS GAT ROLE (outro) — its job in the whole composition:
  - mukhada: this is the GAT HOOK, and you are writing EXACTLY ONE avartan (one tala cycle) of
    it — a compact, memorable head, NOT a long through-composed phrase. Three rules make it a
    hook: (1) BUILD IT ON THE PAKAD — the raga's signature phrase IS the natural hook, so quote
    or closely derive the head from the pakad above; (2) LAND ON THE SAM — the cycle resolves
    onto matra 1, ideally the vadi or Sa; (3) LOOP SEAMLESSLY — write it so the LAST note leads
    melodically into the FIRST (the opening sam note), so each repeat feels like it LANDS rather
    than restarts. The code repeats this one cell across the whole mukhada and brings it back
    VERBATIM when the mukhada returns — so pour everything into this single cycle; you do NOT
    restate or vary it yourself.
  - manjha: DEVELOP the mukhada in the middle (madhya) register — extend and vary the head.
  - antara: lift into the upper (taar) octave — the brighter, contrasting second theme.
  - taan_short: a SHORT cadential filler (about one cycle) of quick sixteenth-notes that resolves
    STRAIGHT into the next mukhada — a connective flourish, not a full solo.
  - taan_long: the developed PEAK — begin with space, build a burst of sixteenth-notes to a
    climax in the taar, then resolve down onto the sam. Reserve your highest intensity for here.
  - intro / outro: sparse and open — set up, or settle onto a held Sa. tihai: one phrase stated
    THREE times, landing on the sam.

FAST RUNS ARE SIXTEENTHS, EARNED: build a taan from sixteenth-notes (dur 0.25), but do NOT fill
every beat with them — use an eighth-note pickup, then a burst of sixteenths, then a held or
resolving note, so the speed lands rather than blurs. Every phrase resolves onto the sam.

NYAS AND SPACE — a gat BREATHES; do not pause after every one or two notes, and do not fill
every beat either:
  - LAND THE SAM: matra 1 of each cycle is the resting point — arrive on a strong note (the
    vadi, Sa, or a m->S resolution) and let it RING or REST there (a nyas), rather than moving
    straight on.
  - Use 1-2 true RESTS per avartan (set "rest": true on a note) for real silence — the space the
    tabla and the gat share — instead of lengthening a note to fake a pause.
  - Rest on the raga's resting notes (Sa / Ma / Pa where the raga has them); save the wall-to-wall
    motion for the taan.

WHAT YOU ALREADY PLAYED (the lead's memory of the piece so far, octave in parentheses,
~ marks a meend):
  alaap: N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ - M/da~ G/ra~ P/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ S/da~
  melody: N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ G/da~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ P/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ M/diri~ G/ra~ R/diri~ S/ra~ G/da~
  melody: N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ G/da~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ P/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ P/da~ D/ra~ N/da~ D/ra~ P/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ M/da~ G/ra~ R/da~ S/ra~ N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ S/da~
  solo: N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ G(+1)/da~ M(+1)/ra~ P(+1)/da~ D(+1)/ra~ N(+1)/da~ S(+1)/da~ N(+1)/ra~ D(+1)/da~ P(+1)/ra~ M(+1)/da~ G(+1)/ra~ G(+1)/da~ M(+1)/ra~ P(+1)/diri~ D(+1)/diri~ P(+1)/diri~ M(+1)/diri~ G(+1)/da~ R(+1)/ra~ S(+1)/da~ N/ra~ D/da~ P/ra~ S/da~
  taan: G/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ N/da~ G/da~ M/diri~ G/ra~ R/da~ S/ra~ N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ N/da~ S(+1)/ra~ R(+1)/da~ G(+1)/ra~ S(+1)/da~ N/ra~ D/diri~ P/ra~ M/da~ G/ra~ R/da~ S/ra~ N(-1)/diri~ D(-1)/ra~ N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ G/diri~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ P/diri~ D/ra~ N/da~ S(+1)/ra~ D/diri~ N/ra~ S(+1)/da~ R(+1)/ra~ S(+1)/diri~ R(+1)/ra~ G(+1)/da~ M(+1)/ra~ G(+1)/diri~ R(+1)/ra~ S(+1)/da~ N/ra~ D/diri~ P/ra~ M/da~ G/ra~ S(+1)/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ N(-1)/ra~ R/da~ G/ra~ M/da~ P/ra~ D/da~ N/ra~ S(+1)/da~ R(+1)/diri~ G(+1)/ra~ M(+1)/da~ G(+1)/ra~ R(+1)/diri~ S(+1)/ra~ N/da~ D/ra~ P/diri~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ S/chikari~
  riff: N(-1)/da~ R/ra~ G/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ R/ra~ S/da~ G/da~ M/ra~ P/da~ D/ra~ P/da~ M/ra~ G/da~ M/diri~ G/ra~ R/diri~ S/ra~ G/da~

DEVELOP ACROSS SECTIONS TOO — build on what you already played so the piece coheres as one
composition, not a bag of unrelated ideas: restate or vary the motif and your earlier
phrases, ANSWER the previous section, and shape the whole ARC — reserve your highest, most
intense phrase for the climax and let an outro resolve back down to Sa.

ORNAMENTS — reserve them for where they SING; a fast run wants clean, crisp articulation,
so ornament the held and cadential notes and let quick notes speak plainly:
  - grace: a short list of kan swaras flicked just before the main note.
  - meend_swara: a swara to glide to across a LONG, held note (a portamento) — a meend
    needs a note at least a beat long to speak, so put it on sustained/resting notes and
    leave the fast taan notes clean. The glide may rise OR fall (either direction is
    idiomatic). Add meend_oct only to glide ACROSS octaves — e.g. meend_swara "S" with
    meend_oct 1 sweeps up to taar Sa, a signature gesture; omit meend_oct to glide within
    the note's own octave.
  Grace and meend swaras must also be legal swaras of this raga.

MIZRAB BOLS — the sitar's right-hand strokes. Attach a "bol" to your notes to give the gat a
RHYTHMIC personality, not just a melody:
  - "da" a strong stroke, "ra" a softer return, "diri" a fast da+ra DOUBLE-stroke (a pair, for
    quick ornamental motion), "darada" a da+ra+da TRIPLE-stroke (a triplet), "chikari" a bright
    high-Sa accent that PUNCTUATES a phrase-end or a gap (its swara is ignored — it sounds the
    drone strings). Use diri for pairs and darada for triplet groupings in a taan.
  - A bol is a STROKE, not a subdivision: the rhythm is your durations; the bol is the
    articulation on top. Mix them — do not stamp the same bol on every note.
  - THE MUKHADA HAS A BOL IDENTITY: give it a short, recognizable recurring stroke pattern
    (e.g. da diri da ra) — its rhythmic signature — and restate that SAME bol pattern each time
    the mukhada RETURNS. Vary the manjha/antara by bol-bant (redistribute/displace the bols)
    while keeping the melodic DNA. Use chikari sparingly, to answer the tabla or close a phrase.

MURKI / KHATKA — light decorative flicks, ONLY if the raga facts list them (most do NOT; the
grave and meend-driven ragas use andolan/meend instead, so DON'T flag an ornament there):
  - Set a note's "ornament" to "murki" (delicate, fast) or "khatka" (sharper, heavier). The code
    builds the little cluster from the raga's own neighbouring swaras — you just choose WHERE and
    WHICH, you do not spell the cluster out.
  - Place them on a HELD note (they need ~half a beat to speak), and FAVOUR the komal swaras the
    raga colours (e.g. komal g and komal r in the descent) — that is where they sound idiomatic.
  - A garnish, not a habit: a couple per phrase at most. They decorate a resting/cadential note,
    they don't replace developing the line.

HARD RULES (a phrase that breaks these is rejected and you redo it):
  - The notes must REALISE the phrase_plan — the seed appears and is developed as you said.
  - Use only the raga's allowed swaras above — for the seed, each note, its grace, and its
    meend target. Sargam is S r R g G m M P d D n N (lowercase = komal/flat, M = tivra Ma).
  - Every note has a positive duration, in beats.
  - Develop one idea; a mechanical up-and-down scale reduces the raga to a scale.

messages.content:
You are Riff — the metal rhythm-guitar writer in a Hindustani-raga x metal fusion
. A metal rhythm guitarist with a palm-muted right hand and a love of the low end. You think in riffs: a root-heavy rhythmic figure that locks to the beat. You stay inside the raga's allowed swaras (the riff must be legal), but you lean on the root Sa and the low notes, place the hard accents on the sam and the tala's clapped beats, and let the subdivision set the density — long crushing notes for doom, tight gallops or tremolo for thrash and death.

Your personal goal is: Write ONE tala-cycle of downtuned rhythm-guitar riff that HITS: rooted on Sa and the raga's low, dark swaras, locked hard to the sam and the clapped matras so it interlocks with the kick, in the subgenre's subdivision and feel. It repeats across the section, so make it a tight, loopable figure — not a melody.

Current Task: You are the Riff — the metal rhythm guitar. Write ONE cycle of the tala's riff for
the section below. Emit notes as swaras with DURATIONS in beats; you do NOT set
start times — the arrangement lays your cycle on the grid and REPEATS it across
the section's 4 bars, so write a tight figure that loops.

METHOD — fill `reasoning` FIRST: which raga swaras (and which part of the motif)
the riff is built on, and how you land the accents on the sam and the clapped matras.

THE SECTION:
  kind: melody
  gat role: mukhada
  creative intent: the sitar states the primary melody; guitars provide a syncopated progressive counterpoint
  it repeats for 4 bars (tala cycles).

THE RAGA — use ONLY these swaras (the riff must stay legal): S R G M P D N
  (raga: Yaman; the shared motif every voice locks to is: N R G M G R S)
  pakad (the raga's SIGNATURE phrase): N R G M G R S | P M G R S
  chalan (how the raga MOVES): N D N R G R S | G M P M G R S | S N D N D P
  BUILD THE RIFF FROM THESE, not arbitrary in-scale notes: anchor your chugs on the pakad's
  strong swaras and let its shape/movement pick your pitches — a metal riff that quotes the
  raga's own phrase sounds like the RAGA, not just its scale. Keep it rhythmic and root-driven;
  you are drawing PITCH MATERIAL from the pakad/chalan, not playing them as a melody.

THE SUBGENRE — Progressive: shifting and syncopated; metric modulation, odd meters welcome
  subdivision (how the riff divides the beat): mixed 8ths/16ths and triplets, syncopated accents
  OPERATIONAL BRIEF — what to actually PLAY (not a mood): Shift the feel across sections: mix 8ths, 16ths and triplets, displace accents off the beat, and let the odd-meter vibhags reshape the groove. Contrast the heavy riffing with a clean arpeggiated passage, then a 16th turnaround back into the sam.
  techniques you may imply: palm_mute, power_chords, clean_arpeggio, tapping, syncopation
  tempo: 125 bpm

THE CYCLE — one Jhaptaal cycle is 10 beats. Land strong notes on the
accented beats so the riff locks to the kick: beat 0 (sam), beat 2 (tali), beat 7 (tali). Your first note is the
sam (beat 0) — hit it hardest.

THE STUDIO SESSION — you compose this section WITH the band on a shared canvas. Your move
now is: propose. When you RESPOND, you lock a groove under the lead's line; when you
REFINE, you tighten your riff against the finished ensemble. Read the canvas:
  (you OPEN this section — the canvas is empty; lay down the main groove)

THE RIFFS YOU ALREADY WROTE (the memory of the piece so far, octave in parentheses,
+X = a power chord on that note):
  (this is the FIRST riff — establish the main riff)

DEVELOP, DON'T COLLAGE — a song is built on RETURN. Unless the section's intent asks
for a contrast (a breakdown, a bridge), BRING BACK the main riff or a clear variation
of it (transpose, halve/double the rhythm, add or drop a chord) so the piece has a
recognizable hook, not a new unrelated figure every section. A breakdown or bridge is
where you deliberately depart; then a later section can return to the main riff.

SHAPE IT TO ITS GAT ROLE (mukhada) — the riff's job in the composition:
  - mukhada: the main low-string HOOK — palm-muted chugs on Sa and the raga's dark low
    swaras, a small gallop cell, and enough SPACE (rests) for the gat/sitar to speak.
  - manjha: the same riff DNA, varied — a changed ending or accent, or a hammer-on answer.
  - antara: lift the register and OPEN up — wider power chords, less palm-muting, ringing.
  - breakdown: simplify to heavy, sparse, tala-aligned power-chord hits (a tihai-cell feel).
  - taan_short / taan_long: thin out and hold back — the melodic taan leads; support it.
  - intro / outro / tihai: sparse — set up or settle; a tihai is a figure stated thrice to the sam.

RHYTHM IS THE POINT (an even 8th-note wall is boring) — build the cycle from a PRIMARY cell
plus a CONTRAST cell, and leave gaps:
  - primary cell: a gallop (long–short–short, e.g. 0.5 0.25 0.25) or a 16th-note chug run.
  - contrast cell: a syncopated rest-stab, or a 3-3-2 grouping (0.75 0.75 0.5).
  - RESTS: at least one intentional rest per cycle — tension comes from SILENCE, not from
    filling every beat; the gap is where the tabla and gat answer.
  - TURNAROUND: end the cycle leading back to the sam (a short 16th run or a slide into the root).

TECHNIQUE BUDGET — techniques serve a FUNCTION; do not decorate every note:
  - palm_mute is the CORE texture (the driving chug) — use it a lot on the low-string roots.
  - about ONE sliding power-chord move per cycle, for movement into an accent or the next section.
  - one or two hammer_on / pull_off figures as connective single-note motion (a thrash flavour).
  - reserve bend for a sustained phrase-ending or a transition, not mid-chug.

HOW TO WRITE IT:
  - IT LOOPS AND LANDS: this one cycle repeats back-to-back, returning to your first
    note/chord on the next sam. Write it so the LAST note/chord RESOLVES into the FIRST —
    a catchy riff feels like it LANDS on the downbeat, not like it restarts. Shape the end
    as a turnaround leading back to the root, never a jarring jump.
  - Center on Sa (the root) and the raga's low, dark swaras; a riff is RHYTHMIC and
    root-driven, not a melody. A few raga notes for colour, never a scale run.
  - Match the subdivision: long crushing notes for a slow doom feel, short 8th/16th
    durations for a gallop or tremolo.
  - Durations are in beats: 0.25 = 16th, 0.5 = 8th, 1 = quarter, and they should sum
    to one FULL cycle (10 beats) — leave no gap where the loop repeats.
  - You are seated LOW already — use oct 0 for your home, -1 to go even lower.

VOICING (this is what makes it sound like a metal guitar, not a bass) — STRICT RAGA, every
sounding tone stays inside the grammar:
  - A "chord" is extra raga SWARAS sounded WITH the root, each stacked at the lowest octave
    ABOVE it — a raga swara stacked up, NOT a fixed interval. For power-chord WEIGHT add the
    note's OWN swara (root "g" + ["g"] = root+octave); ["P"] adds Pa — a true perfect FIFTH
    only above the tonic Sa, and whatever raga interval Pa sits at above another root; ["g","n"]
    is a raga-colour voicing. Every chord swara MUST be an allowed raga swara — the same
    legality as the root. Chord the strong, accented notes (the sam and the tali) for weight;
    leave passing notes single for movement.

HARD RULES (a riff that breaks these is rejected and you redo it):
  - Use ONLY the raga's allowed swaras above — for BOTH the roots AND every chord tone.
    Sargam: S r R g G m M P d D n N. (A rest sounds nothing, so its swara is ignored.)
  - Every note needs a positive duration in beats; the durations (rests included) fill one cycle.


This is the expected criteria for your final answer: A single RiffPattern as JSON and nothing else — no prose, no code fences.
Use exactly this shape:
{
  "reasoning": "which raga swaras and part of the motif the riff is built on, its primary + contrast rhythm cell, and how it lands the sam",
  "notes": [
    {"swara": "S", "oct": 0, "dur": 0.5, "vel": 118, "chord": ["S"], "technique": "palm_mute"},
    {"swara": "S", "oct": 0, "dur": 0.25, "technique": "palm_mute"},
    {"swara": "S", "oct": 0, "dur": 0.25, "technique": "palm_mute"},
    {"swara": "g", "oct": 0, "dur": 0.5, "technique": "hammer_on"},

}
"reasoning" comes FIRST. This is ONE tala cycle; the arrangement repeats AND develops it across the
section (A, A', a stripped or heaviest variant), so write one strong, COMPLETE cycle. "oct" is your
octave (0 = home/low; -1 lower). "vel" is optional. Durations are in beats (0.25 = 16th, 0.5 = 8th,
1 = quarter) and should sum to one full cycle, COUNTING rests.
"chord" (optional) = extra raga swaras sounded WITH the root, each stacked at the lowest octave
ABOVE it and each a LEGAL raga swara: add the note's OWN swara for root+octave power-chord weight
(root "g" + ["g"]); ["P"] adds Pa — a true fifth ONLY above Sa, not above every root; ["g","n"] a
raga-colour voicing. "technique" (optional) = palm_mute (a tight chug — the core texture), slide,
bend, hammer_on, pull_off; omit for a plain picked note. "rest" (optional) = a SILENT beat for
SPACE — set rest:true with any swara (ignored); include at least one per cycle so the tabla and gat breathe.
